body_markdown:
This hub answers 20 of the most common questions HR and operations leaders ask about connecting an applicant tracking system to payroll and onboarding, so new-hire data flows from an accepted offer through the first paycheck without re-entry. Organized into four sections, Fundamentals, Platform and Integration Approaches, Workflow and Implementation, and Compliance and Vendor Selection, these answers cover the mechanics of the data handoff and what to evaluate before choosing a system. Where a connected platform changes the answer, we point to how Asure's own platform, AsureCentral, and its recruiting module, Asure Recruiting, handle that same handoff.


## Fundamentals


### How does an applicant tracking system integrate with payroll and onboarding?


An ATS integrates with payroll and onboarding through a direct data handoff: when a candidate accepts an offer, their record, name, compensation, start date, tax details, gets pushed automatically into the HRIS or payroll system. This eliminates manual re-entry, so payroll setup starts from the accurate, offer-letter-sourced record itself instead of a re-typed copy of it. A[companion piece on connecting recruiting, offer management, and onboarding to eliminate re-entry](https://www.asuresoftware.com/connecting-recruiting-offer-management-and-onboarding-to-eliminate-re-entry/) covers the specific handoff points worth auditing in your own workflow.


### Can new hire data flow automatically from an ATS into payroll?


Yes. When an ATS is natively connected or properly API-integrated with a payroll platform, an accepted offer triggers automated record creation in payroll. The new hire's compensation, tax elections, and start date populate without a payroll administrator manually entering them, which removes both the setup time and the transcription-error risk that comes with retyping the same data a second time.


### What is the difference between a native ATS-payroll integration and an API integration?


A native integration means the ATS and payroll system share the same underlying database, so no sync is required because there's only one record in the first place. An API integration means two separate systems exchange data through a programmatic connection instead. Native integrations tend to be more reliable for payroll-critical fields; API integrations work well too, but require ongoing maintenance and field-mapping audits as either platform gets updated on its own release schedule.


### What does an integrated hiring-to-payroll workflow look like for a small business?


For a small business, an integrated workflow runs in four stages: a candidate applies and is tracked in the ATS, an offer is generated and accepted digitally, the accepted-offer data auto-populates the onboarding record, and payroll configures itself from that same record for the first paycheck. No spreadsheet handoffs, no email attachments, and no re-entry between any of the four stages.


## Platform and Integration Approaches


### Which payroll software integrates best with an HRIS, ATS, and accounting tools?


The strongest integrations exist between platforms built on a shared data layer, where payroll, HRIS, and ATS share one employee record instead of syncing across separate databases. For accounting specifically, look for a certified connector to your accounting platform, whether that's QuickBooks, Sage, or an ERP system, before committing to a vendor. Asure takes this approach with AsureCentral, where payroll, HR, and Asure Recruiting all read from the same employee record rather than passing data between separate applications.


### Which HRIS systems integrate best with payroll, ATS, and benefits systems?


The HRIS platforms that integrate best with payroll, ATS, and benefits are the ones built on a single, unified data model, one record, multiple modules. Middleware-dependent platforms, by contrast, need a separate connection for every pairing, and each one introduces its own sync lag and error risk. When evaluating an HRIS, check whether the vendor owns the payroll and ATS modules directly or relies on third-party partnerships for each one.


### How do HR and payroll platforms typically integrate with an ERP, ATS, and benefits systems?


Most HR and payroll platforms integrate through one of three methods: a native module where all systems share one database, a certified API where the vendor maintains a tested connection to a specific partner, or a middleware or iPaaS layer, tools like Workato or Zapier, that maps fields between otherwise disconnected systems. Native and certified API integrations tend to be the most reliable for payroll-critical data specifically.


### How do top HCM platforms compare on integrations with CRM, ERP, and ATS tools?


Top HCM platforms differ on whether ATS and payroll are native modules or separate partner integrations bolted on afterward; native flow eliminates the sync delays and field-mapping gaps a partner integration introduces. ERP and CRM connections are almost always API or middleware regardless of vendor, so weight native ATS-payroll connectivity most heavily. AsureCentral takes the native route for ATS and payroll, with Asure Recruiting built into the same record; its[HCM partner ecosystem](https://www.asuresoftware.com/hcm-platforms/) covers the broader ERP and CRM connections.


### Is ATS-payroll integration worth the cost for a small business?


For most small businesses, yes. Manual re-entry between recruiting and payroll adds administrative time to every new hire, on top of the error risk that can delay or miscalculate a first paycheck. Asure Recruiting folds that cost into AsureCentral's own onboarding flow instead of pricing it as a separate integration project, which is where a[detailed look at whether applicant tracking systems are worth it for small businesses](https://www.asuresoftware.com/are-applicant-tracking-systems-worth-it/) picks up the return-on-investment question in more depth.


## Workflow and Implementation


### How do I onboard a new hire from an ATS without rekeying their information?


Choose an ATS that's natively integrated with your HRIS or payroll platform, or one that offers a certified API connection covering the fields payroll actually needs. When the offer is accepted, the system automatically creates the employee record downstream, and the new hire completes I-9, W-4, and direct deposit setup digitally, with no HR staff member re-entering data that was already captured during recruiting.


### How do I avoid duplicate data entry between recruiting, onboarding, and payroll?


Select platforms that share a single employee record across recruiting, onboarding, and payroll modules, which is how AsureCentral keeps Asure Recruiting, onboarding, and payroll on one record instead of three. If your systems are separate, a certified integration or a middleware layer can sync records at the offer-acceptance trigger instead of requiring a manual export. The specific fields worth auditing for this are covered in the companion piece on[connecting recruiting, offer management, and onboarding to eliminate re-entry](https://www.asuresoftware.com/connecting-recruiting-offer-management-and-onboarding-to-eliminate-re-entry/) .


### What data fields should transfer from an ATS to payroll at the offer stage?


At minimum: legal name, address, Social Security number, job title, department, compensation rate and frequency, start date, FLSA classification, and manager. Benefits-eligible roles should also transfer benefit plan elections. Any field missing from the transfer becomes a manual re-entry risk, and a potential source of a first-paycheck error.


### How long does it take to set up an ATS-to-payroll integration?


Setup time ranges from same-day, for native or pre-built certified integrations, to considerably longer for custom API or middleware builds that require field-mapping and testing work. A small business using an all-in-one platform can often activate the recruiting-to-payroll data flow during initial platform onboarding itself, with no separate integration project required. Asure Recruiting is already part of that same onboarding inside AsureCentral, so there's no standalone integration project to layer on afterward.


### Does ATS-payroll integration work for hourly and part-time employees, not just salaried hires?


Yes. An integrated workflow handles hourly, part-time, and salaried employees alike, provided the ATS captures pay type (hourly versus salary), rate, and scheduled hours at the offer stage and passes all three fields to payroll. Some ATS platforms default to salary-only offer templates, so verify hourly field support before selecting a vendor. Asure Recruiting passes pay type and rate from the signed offer directly to payroll, so hourly hires flow the same way salaried ones do.


### How does benefits enrollment connect to an ATS-payroll integration?


In a fully integrated workflow, benefits enrollment is triggered by the same offer-acceptance event that creates the payroll record. The new hire receives a benefits enrollment link as part of digital onboarding, and their elections write back to the payroll system so deductions are configured before the first paycheck runs. Platforms without this loop require a separate, manual benefits administration step instead.


### Can an ATS integration handle multi-state payroll tax setup for new hires?


Yes, if the ATS passes the new hire's work-location state to payroll at the offer stage, as Asure Recruiting does before handoff to AsureCentral. The payroll platform then applies the correct state withholding rules automatically. Without that field in the integration, a payroll administrator must manually assign the state tax code, a common source of withholding errors for remote or multi-location hires. A[companion FAQ hub on new-hire payroll tax withholding](https://www.asuresoftware.com/new-hire-payroll-tax-withholding-frequently-asked-questions/) covers the withholding-setup side of this in more depth.


## Compliance and Vendor Selection


### What are the most common errors caused by re-entering new hire data between systems?


The most common errors are incorrect tax withholding from re-transcribed W-4 data, missed direct deposit setup, and compensation entry mistakes, all surfacing on the first paycheck even though the mistake happened earlier. Luna AI, embedded in AsureCentral, flags these mismatches for human review before they reach a paycheck. A[closer look at why most new-hire payroll withholding errors happen before the first paycheck](https://www.asuresoftware.com/why-most-new-hire-payroll-withholding-errors-happen-before-the-first-paycheck/) traces these errors back to the manual data-transfer step between recruiting and payroll specifically.


### What compliance risks arise from disconnected ATS and payroll systems?


Disconnected systems create three recurring compliance risks: I-9 completion delays, incorrect tax withholding from manually re-entered W-4 data, and late new-hire reporting to state agencies. Each carries its own penalty exposure. An integrated ATS-to-payroll workflow automates these triggers instead of relying on manual follow-through. Luna AI adds a review layer on top, surfacing a missing I-9 or an unresolved withholding mismatch for a person to check before a deadline slips.


### What should HR look for in ATS payroll integration when evaluating vendors?


Four criteria matter most: whether the integration is native or third-party (native is lower-maintenance), which data fields actually map (confirm compensation, tax, and benefits fields transfer, not just name and start date), what triggers the sync (offer acceptance or a manual export), and how errors get handled when a field fails to transfer. AsureCentral is a native, single-record system for this reason, so compensation, tax, and benefits fields are already part of the record rather than a separate sync.


### What questions should HR ask an ATS vendor about payroll integration during a demo?


Ask whether the payroll integration is native or API-based, which specific fields transfer at offer acceptance, how integration errors get surfaced and resolved, and whether the vendor can show the actual data flow from offer letter to payroll run live rather than on a slide. Require the live demo, not a description. In an AsureCentral demo, that live flow is Asure Recruiting handing off a signed offer's compensation, start date, and classification fields directly.
